nodes.title: Part 1: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 1. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Which Zero Trust principle states that access should be granted based only on wh?
flashcards.back: Zero Trust's 'Use least privilege access' principle limits user rights with Just-In-Time and Just-Enough-Access (JIT/JEA), risk-based adaptive policies, and data protection. Users get only the permissions they need — nothing more. 'Verify explicitly' means always authenticate using all available signals. 'Assume breach' means design as if a breach has already occurred.

flashcards.front: A security team wants to design a network so that a compromised web server canno?
flashcards.back: Defense in depth uses multiple security layers (network segmentation, firewalls, identity controls, encryption) so that a breach of one layer does not compromise the entire environment. Placing the database in an isolated network segment behind the web tier is a classic defense-in-depth network architecture.

flashcards.front: An employee receives an email that appears to be from IT support asking them to ?
flashcards.back: Phishing is a social engineering attack that uses deceptive emails, messages, or websites to trick users into revealing credentials or clicking malicious links. Spear phishing is a targeted variant. Brute-force attacks guess passwords. Man-in-the-middle attacks intercept network traffic. SQL injection exploits database queries.

flashcards.front: The CIA triad is a foundational security model. An organisation encrypts custome?
flashcards.back: Confidentiality ensures that data is not exposed to unauthorised parties. Encryption is the primary technical control for confidentiality — even if an attacker accesses the storage medium, they cannot read the encrypted data without the key. Integrity protects against unauthorised modification. Availability ensures systems are accessible when needed.

nodes.title: Part 2: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 2. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Which Microsoft Entra ID feature detects risky sign-in behaviours such as sign-i?
flashcards.back: Microsoft Entra ID Protection uses machine learning to detect identity risk signals (anonymous IP, impossible travel, malware-linked IPs, leaked credentials, unfamiliar sign-in properties). It generates risk detections and risk levels (low, medium, high) that Conditional Access policies can act on — for example, requiring MFA for medium-risk sign-ins or blocking high-risk ones.

flashcards.front: A company wants to ensure that Global Administrators only have elevated privileg?
flashcards.back: Privileged Identity Management (PIM) provides Just-In-Time privileged access. Instead of permanently assigned admin roles, PIM makes users 'eligible' for roles. They must explicitly activate the role (provide a justification, get approved, use MFA) and the role expires after a configured time. This dramatically reduces standing privileged access exposure.

flashcards.front: An organisation uses both Microsoft Entra ID and on-premises Windows Server Acti?
flashcards.back: Microsoft Entra Connect synchronises user accounts, groups, and password hashes (or hashes of hashes) from on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID. This enables hybrid identity — users get a single identity that works for both on-premises and cloud resources. It supports Password Hash Sync, Pass-Through Authentication, and Federation.

flashcards.front: A security administrator wants to review whether users still need their current ?
flashcards.back: Microsoft Entra Access Reviews allow administrators (or resource owners) to periodically review and certify user access to groups, applications, and privileged roles. Reviewers confirm or remove assignments. Access Reviews can be scheduled to run automatically, reducing access sprawl and helping meet compliance requirements.

nodes.title: Part 3: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 3. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: The Microsoft Defender portal (security.microsoft.com) consolidates alerts and i?
flashcards.back: Microsoft Defender XDR (Extended Detection and Response) is the integrated security platform that brings together Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Office 365, Defender for Identity, and Defender for Cloud Apps into a single pane of glass at security.microsoft.com. It correlates signals across all these products into unified incidents, enabling faster detection and coordinated response.

flashcards.front: An organisation wants to protect its web applications running on Azure App Servi?
flashcards.back: Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) is a managed rule set that inspects HTTP/HTTPS traffic for OWASP Top 10 attacks (SQL injection, XSS, remote file inclusion, etc.). It can be deployed on Azure Application Gateway, Azure Front Door, or Azure CDN. NSGs operate at the network layer (IP/port) and cannot inspect application-layer attacks. DDoS Protection defends against volumetric attacks.

flashcards.front: A company is concerned about large-scale volumetric network attacks (UDP floods,?
flashcards.back: Azure DDoS Protection Standard provides always-on traffic monitoring and automatic mitigation of DDoS attacks targeting Azure public IP addresses. It defends against volumetric attacks (UDP floods, amplification attacks), protocol attacks (SYN floods), and resource-layer attacks. There is a Basic tier included free with Azure, and Standard (now called Network Protection) provides enhanced mitigation, alerting, and telemetry.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between Azure Firewall and a Network Security Group (NSG)?
flashcards.back: Azure Firewall is a managed, cloud-native firewall with stateful packet inspection, FQDN filtering, threat intelligence integration, and centralised policy management. It operates at a higher level and can control traffic across the entire VNet or multiple VNets. NSGs are lighter-weight, network-layer access control lists (ACLs) applied to subnets or NICs — they filter by source/destination IP, port, and protocol, but cannot do FQDN-based filtering. managed network firewall service that can filter traffic across subscriptions and VNets using FQDN rules; NSGs are simpler network-layer filters (IP/port) applied to subnets or NICs

nodes.title: Part 4: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 4. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A company wants to detect if employees are leaking intellectual property by copy?
flashcards.back: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management detects anomalous user behaviour that may indicate insider threats: data theft by departing employees, sensitive data leaks, security policy violations, and more. It uses machine learning to analyse signals across Microsoft 365 (file downloads, Teams messages, browser activity with Endpoint DLP) and surfaces risk cases for investigation. DLP can block the action, but Insider Risk Management identifies the risky user pattern.

flashcards.front: Which Microsoft Purview feature provides an immutable log of user and admin acti?
flashcards.back: Microsoft Purview Audit (Standard and Premium) records user and admin activity across Exchange Online, SharePoint, Teams, OneDrive, and other Microsoft 365 services. Audit Standard retains logs for 180 days; Audit Premium extends this to 1 year (or 10 years with an add-on) and adds intelligent insights. Administrators can search the audit log for forensic investigation and compliance evidence.

flashcards.front: An organisation needs to ensure that employees in the legal department cannot co?
flashcards.back: Information barriers in Microsoft Purview are policies that prevent specific segments of users from communicating with each other in Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive. They are used in regulated industries (financial services, law firms, government) to prevent conflicts of interest, insider trading, and breaches of fiduciary duty. Unlike communication compliance (which reviews after-the-fact), information barriers block the communication from occurring.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance helps organisations detect messages i?
flashcards.back: Communication compliance uses machine learning classifiers and keyword policies to surface messages in Teams, Exchange, and Viva Engage that may contain harassment, threatening language, adult content, or regulatory violations (like sharing investment advice). A compliance reviewer examines flagged messages and takes action. It is a supervisory/review tool, not a blocking tool like DLP. inappropriate language, or regulatory violations (such as stock tip sharing)
